proof_summary: The defining sum gives the recurrence \(a(n+1)=(2^n-1)a(n)+2^{\binom{n+1}{2}}\); for odd \(p\), Fermat's theorem gives the base value \(a(2p-1)\equiv1\pmod p\), since every nonfinal summand contains \(2^{2(p-1)}-1\) while the final power is congruent to 1. Fermat also makes both powers in the recurrence invariant under a shift by \(2(p-1)\) (the triangular exponents differ by a multiple of \(p-1\)), so induction propagates the congruence, while \(p=2\) follows from the recurrence showing all positive-index terms are odd.
